Free to start, live in minutes.", "targetKeyword": "website builder for photographers", "category": "Industries", "bodyHtml": "

Most website builders hand photographers a generic template and a stock photo of a camera. You spend a weekend dragging blocks around, and the result still looks like everyone else's site. Kodely works differently: you describe your photography business in plain English, and it writes a real Vite + React + TypeScript app around it — not a drag-and-drop mockup, actual component code you can view, copy, and keep editing by chat.

What Photographer Websites Actually Need

A photography site has a narrower job than most small-business sites, but it has to nail a few things or it doesn't work at all:

  • A strong visual portfolio. The gallery is the pitch. If it's cluttered or slow, nothing else on the page matters.
  • Services and packages. Weddings, portraits, events, commercial work — whatever you shoot, priced or at least scoped clearly.
  • About and style. Clients are hiring a point of view, not just a camera. A short, specific about section does more than a long one.
  • A way to actually reach you. A booking or inquiry form that captures what the client needs before you ever get on a call.

The Must-Have Sections, Built In

When you describe a photography site to Kodely, it structures the generated app around these sections by default:

SectionWhat it does
HeroYour name or studio name, a tagline, and a lead visual area
GalleryA grid or masonry layout section for your portfolio
Services / PackagesCards or a table laying out what you shoot and how it's structured
AboutYour story and shooting style, written to match your voice
Contact / Book a SessionA contact form UI for inquiries

A Real Example Prompt for a Photography Site

You don't need a design brief or a spec sheet. A prompt like this is enough to get a full first draft:

"Build a portfolio site for a wedding and portrait photographer named Maren Lucas, based in Portland. Moody, editorial style — dark background, serif headings, lots of white space. Include a hero section with my name and a tagline, a gallery section with a grid of image placeholders, a services section with three packages (Elopement, Full Wedding Day, Portrait Session), an about section, and a contact section with a Book a Session form asking for name, email, event date, and event type."

Kodely turns that into a working app in minutes, with a live preview rendering the actual compiled site as it's generated.

What Kodely Generates — and the Honest Part About Your Photos

Here's the part worth being direct about: Kodely doesn't handle real photo uploads or image hosting yet. The gallery section it builds is a real, styled component — proper grid layout, spacing, hover states, responsive behavior — but it ships with placeholder images. After your site is live, you'll need to add your own photos yourself.

Same honesty applies to the contact form. Kodely builds a working UI for a "Book a Session" form with the fields you ask for. It is not a booking or payment system — there's no calendar sync, no deposit collection, no backend behind it yet. Think of it as the front end for your booking process, not the process itself.

What you do get is real: actual .tsx component files built on Kodely's foundation codebase of hand-built UI primitives, not a locked-down template. You can view and copy the generated source in-app any time.

Customizing Your Site in Chat

Once the first draft is live in preview, refine it the same way you built it — by describing the change. "Make the gallery three columns on desktop and one on mobile," "swap the serif headings for something more modern," "add a fourth package called Engagement Session" — each request edits the real components behind the scenes. Every successful generation is saved as a checkpoint, so if a change doesn't land the way you wanted, rolling back to the previous version is free.

Publishing Live

When the site looks right, one click on Publish puts it live at yourname.kodely.site — free, included, no separate hosting step to configure. Before anything goes live, Kodely scans the build for accidentally leaked secrets or API keys. Custom domains aren't supported yet, so your site lives on the kodely.site subdomain for now.

FAQ

Do I need to know how to code?

No. You describe the site in chat and Kodely writes the code. If you do know React, you can view and copy the generated files and keep working from there.

Can I upload my own photos?

Not directly through Kodely yet. The gallery section is built with placeholder images that you'll replace with your own after the site is generated and published.

Does the booking form actually take bookings?

It captures the UI and the fields you specify, but there's no backend, payment processing, or calendar behind it yet. It's a front end you can connect a real booking process to later.

What does it cost?

New accounts get 750 free credits, no credit card required. Credits are metered from real AI cost, and a build that fails to compile is never charged. When you need more, top-ups run $9 for 500 credits, $40 for 2,500 credits, and $90 for 6,000 credits — credits never expire.

Can I export the code?

You can view and copy the generated source files in-app. There's no zip export yet.

Ready to see your own portfolio take shape? Build your photography site free and have a live draft in minutes.

No. You describe the site in chat and Kodely writes the code. If you do know React, you can view and copy the generated files and keep working from there.

Can I upload my own photos?

Not directly through Kodely yet. The gallery section is built with placeholder images that you'll replace with your own after the site is generated and published.

Does the booking form actually take bookings?

It captures the UI and the fields you specify, but there's no backend, payment processing, or calendar behind it yet. It's a front end you can connect a real booking process to later.

What does it cost?

New accounts get 750 free credits, no credit card required. Credits are metered from real AI cost, and a build that fails to compile is never charged. When you need more, top-ups run $9 for 500 credits, $40 for 2,500 credits, and $90 for 6,000 credits — credits never expire.

Can I export the code?

You can view and copy the generated source files in-app. There's no zip export yet.
